raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With NIXL 1.5.0, a pull that fails with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` leaves the UCX endpoint to that prefill worker failed for good, so every later read between the two workers fails until one side restarts or the peer is evicted. The decode worker releases a failed peer only when `check_remote_metadata` reports its metadata missing, which it never does here. This adds a second release trigger next to that check: a peer is also released once two requests to it fail with no completed read in between, so the existing drain, backoff and re-handshake path builds a fresh connection.

Related: #55471 (added the invalid-peer path and the metadata check), #61238 (invalidates peers whose READ has stalled; touches the same lines), #61499 (keeps the engine up through these failures with HiSparse).

## Claims

- Confirmed missing local metadata releases the peer after the first failed read, unchanged from #55471.
- When two requests to a pull peer fail with recorded transport failures and no completed read in between, the peer is released once its reads drain, and the next read to it re-handshakes. A completed read resets the count, so a single failed request keeps the peer.
- A release that repeats within 60 s backs off from 1 s to 60 s before the next re-handshake, for either trigger; reads to the peer fail fast meanwhile.
- KV lease expiry and reads rejected while a peer drains are not transport failures and do not count. Push mode is unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** The #55471 tests are unchanged, including `test_recovery_requires_confirmed_missing_metadata`. `test_failed_reads_release_peer_with_loaded_metadata` fails two requests with the peer's metadata still loaded: the first keeps the peer, the second releases every rank of it. `test_completed_read_resets_failed_requests` checks that a completed read clears the count. With `_PEER_FAILED_REQS_BEFORE_RELEASE = 99` the first new test fails; with `1` four tests fail, including the #55471 cases where metadata is still present.

```text
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
# main 8c60cf07b3:  375 passed, 3 failed
# this branch:      377 passed, 3 failed (2 tests added)
```

The 3 failures are the same on both: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]`, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None]` and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` start an engine and need a GPU and a gated model download.

<details>
<summary>Production trace, measured on df2c1c9172 (release on the first failed request)</summary>

GLM-5.3 on H100, P/D with NIXL 1.5.0 (UCX backend), vLLM main `d6aca837c3` plus three unrelated PRs and #61499. The change ran as a startup patch on decode engines started after 17:17 UTC on 2026-10-13.

| decode engine | after its first failed read to a prefill worker |
|---|---|
| without the change | the link failed every later read over it: two engines of one decode group failed 101 requests against two prefill workers between 18:46 and 19:33 UTC |
| with the change | one failed request; the peer released 50 ms later and a fresh handshake (`NIXL compatibility check passed`) 5 s after that (20:16 UTC). Two peers released this way at 18:24 UTC failed no further reads through 18:26 UTC |

With the count trigger, the same incident fails one more request, the next read over the failed endpoint, before the release.

</details>

## Details

Path of the failure on main, decode side, pull mode:

1. A decode worker reads a request's KV from a prefill worker. The UCX error callback fires for that endpoint (`nixlUcxEp::err_cb`, `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp` in NIXL 1.5.0) and moves it from `CONNECTED` to `FAILED`. Nothing moves it back; only `loadRemoteConnInfo`, run when the remote agent's metadata is added, creates a `CONNECTED` endpoint.
2. Every later read posted on a `FAILED` endpoint returns `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` (`nixlUcxEp::read` and `postSgl` call `checkTxState`). The request fails, and `_handle_failed_transfer` records the remote engine in `_failed_remote_engines`.
3. `_cleanup_remote_engines` calls `check_remote_metadata` on the peer's agents without descriptors. `nixlAgent::checkRemoteMD` then only checks that the remote section exists locally, which it does, so the peer is kept.
4. The next request routed to that prefill worker reads over the same `FAILED` endpoint and fails at step 2.

The change keeps the metadata check in step 3 and adds a second trigger after it. `_failed_reqs_by_engine` holds, per peer, the requests that failed since its last completed read; `_cleanup_remote_engines` marks a peer invalid once it holds `_PEER_FAILED_REQS_BEFORE_RELEASE` (2) of them, or as before when its metadata is missing. The release path keeps its logic: reads to the peer are rejected until in-flight reads drain, its agents are removed, and the next read re-handshakes.

Why two failed requests: an invalidated peer rejects every new read while its reads drain, so releasing on one failure would cost a few seconds of recomputes for an error that might not repeat. A failed endpoint fails every later read (101 requests in the trace above), so on a dead connection the second failure arrives with the next read, at the cost of one more failed request. Requests count once however many of their transfers fail. There is no NIXL call that reports endpoint health, so one failure with metadata loaded cannot tell the two cases apart. Missing metadata already confirms stale state, so that trigger does not wait.

Not a duplicate. Open PRs found with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for "check_remote_metadata", "nixl remote disconnect", "nixl rehandshake" and "nixl invalid peer": #61238 invalidates a peer whose READ stays in `PROC` past a timeout, which never records a failed transfer; #60279 handles stale P2P tiering registrations. Neither releases a peer after failed reads.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Thanks @NickLucche. I think we should preserve the confirmed-missing-metadata recovery path from #55471: once NIXL has dropped the local peer metadata, the cached connector state is already stale, so waiting for a second failed request does not add confidence.

#61500 addresses an additional case: the metadata still exists, but the underlying connection is unusable. I would handle that as a separate recovery trigger, reusing the existing drain, cleanup, backoff and re-handshake logic. For that case, I agree that the two-request threshold needs more evidence. This would extend recovery coverage without delaying the already-confirmed invalidation case, and we should retain the existing missing-metadata regression tests.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This releases the peer on the first transfer error, and while it drains and re-handshakes, every read to that prefill worker fails fast. So one transient error costs a few seconds of recomputes.
Would it make sense to define a threshold, say two or more failures before the release?

inline_comments.body: Makes sense, added in 66091e233. A peer is released once two requests to it fail with no completed read in between (`_PEER_FAILED_REQS_BEFORE_RELEASE = 2`), and a completed read resets the count, so an isolated error keeps the peer. On a dead UCX endpoint every later read fails at post, so the second failure arrives with the next read and costs one more failed request before the release. A request counts once however many of its transfers fail, and reads rejected while a peer drains do not count. `test_single_failed_request_keeps_peer` and `test_completed_read_resets_failed_requests` cover it; the description is updated to match.

Thanks @NickLucche. I think we should preserve the confirmed-missing-metadata recovery path from #55471: once NIXL has dropped the local peer metadata, the cached connector state is already stale, so waiting for a second failed request does not add confidence.

#61500 addresses an additional case: the metadata still exists, but the underlying connection is unusable. I would handle that as a separate recovery trigger, reusing the existing drain, cleanup, backoff and re-handshake logic. For that case, I agree that the two-request threshold needs more evidence. This would extend recovery coverage without delaying the already-confirmed invalidation case, and we should retain the existing missing-metadata regression tests.
